version.version_or_commit: RFC 5545, Standards Track, September 2009; recurrence gap text corrected by verified Erratum 4271 (S12)
version.governing_condition_default_exception: UID is the persistent component identifier; RECURRENCE-ID is the original slot and retains its value type; DTSTART/RRULE/RDATE minus EXDATE defines the set, EXDATE wins, and unsynchronized DTSTART/RRULE is undefined. For TZID DTSTART, UNTIL is UTC. DATE-TIME folds select the first instant and explicit gaps use the pre-gap offset. Apply Erratum 4271 (S12) to RRULE-generated gap candidates. Section 3.2.20 covers unknown value-type tokens, not general property-name preservation; sections 3.8.8.1–.2 allow generic consumers to ignore IANA/X-name properties. The RRULE grammar permits UNTIL or COUNT, not both, and COUNT includes DTSTART as its first occurrence.

version.version_or_commit: RFC 5545, Standards Track, September 2009; recurrence gap text corrected by verified Erratum 4271 (S12)
version.governing_condition_default_exception: UID is the persistent component identifier; RECURRENCE-ID is the original DTSTART slot and has the same value type and local-time form as master DTSTART. The recurrence set is DTSTART plus RRULE/RDATE minus EXDATE; exclusions win, duplicates collapse, and a DTSTART/RRULE mismatch is undefined. A TZID references a matching VTIMEZONE; recurring VTIMEZONE rules must cover every recurrence. With TZID DTSTART, UNTIL is UTC DATE-TIME; COUNT and UNTIL are mutually exclusive and COUNT includes DTSTART. DATE-TIME folds choose the first instant and explicit gaps use the pre-gap offset; Erratum 4271 changes generated-gap handling and is recorded under S12. §3.2.20 requires preservation of unknown value-type token data only; IANA/X-name properties may be ignored by generic applications.
version.applicability: Primary file-format contract for the requested adapter; it does not select the product subset, duplicate policy, or guarantee cross-reader behavior.

version.released_version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, October 2018
version.governing_condition_default_exception: BagIt 1.0 requires at least one payload manifest and each manifest lists every payload file exactly once; completeness requires listed files and every payload file to be listed, while validity additionally requires checksums to verify. Creation/validation tools MUST support SHA-256 and SHA-512 and SHOULD enable SHA-512 by default. Extra tag files are allowed but generic implementations ignore their contents unless validating their listed bytes. The format addresses corruption, not active attacks. Filesystem normalization and Windows/Unix naming can affect paths.
version.applicability: Portable, inspectable package per deposit; does not natively provide corrected-version history or curatorial completeness.

version.released_version_or_commit: OCFL 1.1 series; latest listed release 1.1.1, tag 1.1.1, commit c3f88b3 (release record S04)
version.governing_condition_default_exception: Versions are continuous directories and expected immutable; each version's content files must be referenced by its inventory manifest. The stable object id must not change. Inventories map digests to stored paths and version states to logical paths, use UTF-8 JSON and slash paths with path safety constraints, and require matching digest sidecars written after inventory edits. An optional logs directory can hold local action records whose format is outside the spec.
version.applicability: Filesystem-native structured version history; suitable if the gallery needs accumulated/reconstructable history, with greater update and validator discipline than one BagIt deposit per correction.

version.released_version_or_commit: PREMIS v3.0, Library of Congress page marks full document updated November 2015
version.governing_condition_default_exception: PREMIS distinguishes Objects, Events, Rights, Agents; fixity records digest algorithm/value, while an observed check and its result/date are recorded as an Event/outcome. Event identifier, type and datetime are mandatory in the data model. Some backup-copy actions may instead be kept in system logs/audit trails.
version.applicability: Design basis for a compact readable identity/custody log. The recommendation is PREMIS-inspired, not a claim of formal conformance or a new preservation platform.

version.version: PostgreSQL major version 17 documentation; target Read Committed
conditions_and_exceptions: The assignment's conditional DO UPDATE WHERE may deliberately skip an older or equal timestamp; that skip is documented by S1.
The upsert behavior does not remove independent statement or transaction errors.
version.applicability: Supports use of the required Read Committed isolation for concurrent writes to the unique device_id key; the monotonic timestamp result is an inference from applying S1's strict condition to the current conflicting row.

version.version_or_release: Specification 700-713–16; revision history records 2016-09-30 changes; current index calls this the most recent posted PDF. No commit identifier.
version.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: LOC purchasing; plastic/metal collection storage containers; thermal-transfer printer; excludes rare/high-value and photographic uses; disclaims commercial endorsement. It specifies face stock selected by user, vendor-compatible ribbon and identified printer. Initial bond uses a 7-day dwell at 23°C/50% RH; accelerated bond and curl/lift exposure is 80°C/50% RH for 28 days, followed by 24 hours at 23°C/50% RH for bond testing. It separately evaluates bond, curl/lift/ooze, print fastness, and abrasion. §2.5 also states a performance requirement for normal use over the life of the object, but the accelerated protocol itself gives no storage-year conversion.
version.applicability: A procurement/test-design and traceability precedent only. It provides no case-specific suitability, safety endorsement, acceptance threshold, or lifetime conversion.
